newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich sees one-in-three chance for tobacco pact.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich sees one-in-three chance for tobacco pact.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich on Tuesday said there was a one-in-three chance that a broad settlement of tobacco-related lawsuits would be reached and then be approved by Congress.
The Georgia Republican said that was his personal opinion and that he set those odds because "there's some very, very big issues still out there."

Tobacco companies and state attorneys general are in negotiations aimed at settling tobacco-related lawsuits. Industry officials have indicated they may be willing to accept new federal controls as part of an overall settlement in return for concessions such as protection from future litigation. Any broad pact would require congressional approval.
